title: The histone variant H2A.Z regulates sex differences in Alzheimer’s disease pathophysiology
title_zh: 组蛋白变体H2A.Z调控阿尔茨海默病的性别差异
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) disproportionately affects women, yet mechanisms underlying this sex difference remain unclear. Histone variants are overrepresented components of aging neuronal chromatin, but their contribution to AD is unknown. Here, we identify the histone variant H2A.Z as a sex-specific regulator of AD in the postmortem human hippocampus and in 5xFAD mice. H2A.Z occupancy decreased in female but increased in male AD patients. In females, reduced H2A.Z occupancy at the transcription start site (TSS) occurred despite increased total H2A.Z, indicating that H2A.Z is redistributed to sites of lower H2A.Z occupancy. Similar sex-dependent alterations were observed in 5xFAD mice over disease progression. Whereas H2A.Z.1 depletion improved memory and AD pathology in females at early and late disease stages, it impaired memory in male mice at early stages and improved memory in late stages. Together, these data identify H2A.Z as a regulator of sex- and stage-dependent AD outcomes, with implications for the sex-specific therapeutic targeting of chromatin factors.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（AD）对女性的影响更为显著，但导致这种性别差异的机制尚不清楚。组蛋白变体在衰老神经元染色质中占比过高，但其在AD中的作用尚未明了。在本研究中，我们在尸检人类海马和5xFAD小鼠中发现组蛋白变体H2A.Z是AD的性别特异性调控因子。H2A.Z在女性AD患者中的占据率下降，而在男性中则上升。在女性中，尽管总H2A.Z水平升高，但转录起始位点（TSS）处的H2A.Z占据率下降，表明H2A.Z被重新分布到占据率较低的位点。类似的性别依赖性改变在5xFAD小鼠的疾病进展过程中也被观察到。H2A.Z.1的缺失在早期和晚期疾病阶段均能改善女性的记忆和AD病理，但在早期阶段对男性小鼠的记忆产生负面影响，晚期则改善记忆。综上所述，这些数据表明H2A.Z是调控性别和疾病阶段相关AD结果的关键因子，对针对染色质因子的性别特异性治疗具有重要意义。
